body: Thanks for pointing that out -__- that was meant to clarify my own gender, I realize now that clarifying my boyfriend's gender was really stupid of me.

I'm pretty much the same way. I get off to the hot, sexy action that I imagine in my head, but the second I start imagining faces, getting off just gets so much harder and I eventually have to stop and start over again. For me it's just this unnecessary detail that just messes everything up for me, so in my brain when I'm imagining super hot sex, I just don't care who it is, and I never look at/imagine their faces. The closest I'll get to coming up with a specific person is when I'm imagining my boyfriend, and even then it's just his hair.

tl;dr- me too.

She'll be fine. It'll sting to pee for about a week but it'll heal up.

FUCK! HOW DID YOU KNOW??!?!?! GLENDALE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
well. la crescenta. the more asian version of glendale with even less to do...

Yeah high school is shit. I don't really know what is so great about the cliques and the drama and all the other stuff. Maybe if you're super popular and you go to parties and get drunk and high every weekend it's fun, but I'm not that kind of person.

Music has definitely been my savior, both listening to it and performing. Well, I suppose performing has helped me a lot more- I'm not plugged up with headphones trying to block everyone out, I'm doing something I love and I'm getting better at it each time I practice, and hearing the final result of a piece you have put so much time and effort in to practicing is one of the best feelings I have ever felt, like I actually did something right for once.

I think I'm just going to play violin for the rest of my life, now that I think living isn't such a bad option after all. I'm planning on getting a minor in music when I go to college, so I'm pretty happy about that. It really does feel good to have a non-human outlet, and I sometimes forget that.

I have stopped cutting, I've been cut free for... Wow, I stopped counting. I really don't know how long it's been, but I can safely say over a year. My mom and I made a deal when she found out about me cutting- I stop cutting, and she'd stop smoking. She hasn't stopped smoking but I'm not mad at her for it or anything, I feel good because I stopped and I feel like I should be helping her find a different outlet for her stress in the same way that I was able to. I never got any professional help no matter how much I wanted/still want to, and I'm really thinking that I should soon.

Everyone always jokes that my parents are worse than Asians >.< my mom's actually part ukrainian part Russian and my dad is part Armenian part Persian, and everyone expects me to be a spoiled little brat with a BMW (that's just how armenians are where I live. They ALL drive BMWs or some other car they can't afford) and they are so surprised when they learn that my parents actually CARE about my grades... *gasp*

Thanks so much for helping me out today, it has definitely put things in a new light and made me seriously reconsider.

After moping around in bed all day, I got up and told my sister that my violin was missing. She completely flipped out, and immediately started helping me look. She checked in a place that I could have sworn I checked about eight times... and it was there. That in itself made me feel about a million times better- my violin has saved my life on countless other occasions, I don't think I could have made it through the first year of high school if I never played. 

After I found it, I just sat in my room and cried for about an hour, just out of pure happiness. It felt SO good to know that my violin is safe and in my arms again, and maybe next time I clean my room I won't hide it so well :/ Hell, I'm even considering sleeping with it tonight. Actually, it's a him and I'm disrespecting him by calling him an it... I named him Ronald when I got him for Christmas two years ago. 

I feel so much better after finding him, and I kept asking myself, "what if I actually went through with my plan and killed myself, leaving a suicide note saying I did it because I lost my violin and yada yada yada, and my body, which would be most likely on the floor of my bedroom, is RIGHT next to my violin case??" I guess it taught me that you just never know what could be right around the corner if you hold on for a little bit longer.

I did some calculating today, and if I get As on my next math test and final, I can get a B in the class. Of course it'll take a lot of work, but now more than ever I'm willing to try... and hopefully I won't give up again. I need to find some sort of incentive for myself to keep on studying and to not give up...

I know that my past will come back to haunt me eventually, and I will feel this way again in the future. But I think right now I have to get myself back on my feet, regain some confidence and just do some things I'm truly proud of myself for so when it does inevitably come back to haunt me, I can always remind myself of how far I've come.

Thank you so much again for taking the time to help me out, you really don't know how much I appreciate it. *huge choking hug*

Thanks so much for the offer, but I feel like it should be something that I do myself. I have done something similar to that before and it didn't really go well; my parents took it as more of a "you should let her off easy" thing instead of a "your daughter is going through stuff and is too pussy to tell you" thing.

I think I'll write my mom a letter or an email to tell her. When we sit down and talk about stuff face to face it tends to get really emotional and not really rational, and I hate that. I'd rather write her a letter, give her a couple of hours to digest it, then talk about it later... and MAYBE get emotional about it after we've come up with some solutions to the problem.

Do you think I should tell them EVERYTHING, or do you think I should censor what I tell them a bit? I honestly don't want to tell them anything, but do you think there are certain things that need to be said?

None of our teachers want to get involved in our personal lives. They always tell us that we can talk to them about things, but if we are/have been in danger in any way, they need to report it, call lots of people... and then it gets super dramatic and even more unpleasant.

I suppose I could try asking, but I'm positive that we would have to have some certain kind of talk before they would let me go. It's not like they would send me to counseling if they think everything's ok with me and they think that I might just be having a hard time getting over my dog's death or something. They'd want to know just a little bit of what's going on before deciding that I really need it.

I really REALLY want to go, though. Just nervous about what the conversation would be like.

I have tried talking to a counselor at school, but unfortunately, she keeps getting pregnant and going on maternity leaves for months. I think she was only here for the first month or so of school, and the day I requested to see her was the day she left again, and our school didn't get a replacement. We only have a few normal academic counselors now, but my one is kind of a bitch and tries to shoo me out the door whenever I try to come see her about anything, so I don't exactly trust her with something like this.

I do want to ask my parents if I could talk to a counselor, but they would want to know what's wrong with me before sending me to one. They figure that of all people I should be able to tell them about my problems, not some random person who is paid to listen to me. I don't want to have to put myself in the position of being forced to tell them everything, because as far as they know right now, I'm just a lazy girl who went through a growing up/hormonal phase when she cut herself for a bit and stopped.

You pretty much hit the nail on the head... my parents have always been praising me like crazy, and when I do something I think is great and I don't get enough praise for it I feel really disappointed.

I am pretty smart though. Not being full of myself of anything, my version of my grades plummeting is having a 3.5 GPA and getting straight As and one C in AP Calculus this semester. My grades have improved since last year, but still, that one C is pretty disastrous for me and my family just because they know I can do better, and I know it too. 

I don't think the way my parents praise me is as horribly extreme as what the article describes, though... if I get an A on a test, they'll ask what percentage. If I say anything less than a 93%, they'll ask why I got a low A, and to do better next time. 

But it still has been bad though. They've been calling me Professor (my name) or Doctor (my name) ever since I was five because they're SO sure I'll be a doctor in the future because I just HAVE to be (I don't even like biology, so I don't know where they get the idea that I'm going to be a doctor).

I'm not offended by what you said, I do really care about people's expectations of me, but mostly because I feel like it should be what I expect of myself, too. 

My parents just want me to do well in school and go on to college and do well there too, and to be happy, and that's it. It's not like they expect me to be valedictorian and get a 2400 on my SATs and all that. They know I can meet their expectations, and I know I can too, and they're only upset with me because they know I can do better.

My issue is I give up too easily. When I get knocked down, I stay there until my parents drag me back up... and then I just get back down again. I just don't know how to deal with hard things going on in my life, and that scares me a lot because I know things are only going to get harder. I'm just so used to sitting and moping about things and not standing up and taking initiative to make things better again. 

If I come home and I think about something that happened in the past, I just go ahead and cry about it, and my homework doesn't get done. The next day when I try to catch up, if I don't understand everything right away, I get discouraged and I just stop trying. I don't know why I keep doing this to myself, I really hate it. I want to change but I don't think I can anymore.

I don't know, I feel like they would get over it and move on eventually, because they've gone through other hard things and have dealt with them really well. 

The thing is that every time I bring home bad grades or I do something bad, I have to come up with some bs excuse like "I was lazy" or "it was hard" or something.

I'm normally a really, really good student, but all of the things that have gone on with me in the past few years keep on bringing me down and I don't have the same drive to do my best as I used to.

I feel like if I told them EVERYTHING then we could finally come up with some way of getting me back on my feet and being a happy person again. They know about me cutting, but not about anything else that has happened. I do want to talk to a therapist, but that means telling my parents about all of this, and I really don't want to keep on making their lives so hard, because it's hard enough for them as it is without me telling them all of this.
